subject: Physics
topic: Vectors & Coordinate Frames: Components, Resultants & Geometric Invariants
title: Grade 9 Olympiad Physics Core 1B Phenomenological Reconstruction: Vectors & Coordinate Frames

reconstruction_cycles.standard_derivation: Choose +x East. Cart moves +7 m, -11 m, +2 m. Displacement is Delta x = (+7) + (-11) + (+2) = -2 m (2 m West). Total distance is d = |+7| + |-11| + |+2| = 20 m.

phenomenological_reconstruction.conceptual_pivot: The positive sign does not mean 'good' or 'increasing'; it designates alignment with a declared reference arrow. Flipping the reference axis (+x West) transforms the displacements to -7 m, +11 m, -2 m, yielding Delta x = +2 m (still 2 m West). Physical displacement is completely invariant under choice of axis orientation.
phenomenological_reconstruction.scalar_vs_vector_boundary: Distance accumulates total odometer path regardless of heading (scalar d = 20 m). Displacement preserves the net spatial translation between origin and terminal location (vector Delta x = 2 m West).

limiting_boundary_checks.physical_consequence: Displacement magnitude equals total distance traveled: |Delta x| = d.

limiting_boundary_checks.limit: Closed circuit (returns exactly to starting coordinate)
limiting_boundary_checks.physical_consequence: Net displacement vanishes identically (Delta x = 0), while path distance d > 0.

reconstruction_cycles.standard_derivation: Two vectors A and B act at angle theta. Analytical resultant: R^2 = A^2 + B^2 + 2 A B cos theta. Extreme bounds: theta = 0 deg gives R_max = A + B; theta = 180 deg gives R_min = |A - B|; theta = 90 deg gives Pythagoras R = sqrt(A^2 + B^2).

phenomenological_reconstruction.conceptual_pivot: Imagine two students pulling a tethered ring with dynamometers of calibrated forces A and B. When pulling parallel, tensions add directly to maximum A + B. As one student walks in an arc around the ring, the net pull smoothly decreases. At 90 deg, the right-angle Pythagorean diagonal emerges. At 180 deg, they pull in direct opposition, yielding minimum tension |A - B|.
phenomenological_reconstruction.geometric_closure: For three vectors in equilibrium (A + B + C = 0), the three arrows must form a closed triangle head-to-tail, proving C = -(A + B).

limiting_boundary_checks.physical_consequence: cos(0) = 1 => R = sqrt(A^2 + B^2 + 2AB) = A + B (algebraic sum).
cos(180) = -1 => R = sqrt(A^2 + B^2 - 2AB) = |A - B| (algebraic cancellation).

limiting_boundary_checks.limit: Equal magnitude orthogonal forces (A = B, theta = 90 deg)
limiting_boundary_checks.physical_consequence: cos(90) = 0 => R = A sqrt(2), bisecting the angle at exactly 45 deg.

reconstruction_cycles.phenomenon: Velocity Change Vector at Constant Speed (Geometric Turn)
reconstruction_cycles.standard_derivation: Particle moves with speed v turning through angle theta: v_i = v i, v_f = v cos theta i + v sin theta j. Change in velocity is Delta v = v_f - v_i = v(cos theta - 1) i + v sin theta j. Magnitude: |Delta v| = sqrt(v^2 (cos theta - 1)^2 + v^2 sin^2 theta) = sqrt(2 v^2 (1 - cos theta)) = 2v sin(theta/2).

phenomenological_reconstruction.conceptual_pivot: Novices confuse change in speed with change in velocity. Speed is constant (|v_i| = |v_f| = v), but velocity direction rotates. Reconstruct by drawing both vectors from a single point: Delta v is the directed vector pointing from the tip of v_i to the tip of v_f.
phenomenological_reconstruction.dynamic_necessity: Because Delta v != 0, Newton's second law dictates that a net force and impulse J = m Delta v must act continuously toward the interior of the turn to bend the trajectory.

limiting_boundary_checks.physical_consequence: sin(0) = 0 => |Delta v| = 0 (no acceleration, uniform straight-line motion).
|Delta v| = 2v sin(45 deg) = v sqrt(2), directed at 45 deg inward.
|Delta v| = 2v sin(90 deg) = 2v (doubled velocity change, antiparallel).

reconstruction_cycles.phenomenon: The Observer as the Subtracted Vector (Galilean Relative Shift)
reconstruction_cycles.standard_derivation: Object A moves at v_A; observer B moves at v_B. Relative velocity of A with respect to B is v_{AB} = v_A - v_B. In components: v_{AB,x} = v_{Ax} - v_{Bx}, v_{AB,y} = v_{Ay} - v_{By}.

phenomenological_reconstruction.conceptual_pivot: To see what observer B sees, we must bring observer B to rest. Bringing B to rest requires applying an opposing velocity -v_B to B. By Galilean invariance, we must apply this exact same transformation velocity -v_B to every other object in the universe.
phenomenological_reconstruction.relative_reality: Object A thus possesses its own ground velocity v_A plus the observer correction -v_B: v_{AB} = v_A + (-v_B) = v_A - v_B. If both objects travel with identical velocity vectors, the relative velocity vanishes identically.

limiting_boundary_checks.physical_consequence: v_{AB} = 0; objects appear stationary relative to each other.
v_{AB} = v_A; recovers standard ground-frame velocity.

limiting_boundary_checks.limit: Head-on collinear collision (v_A = v i, v_B = -u i)
limiting_boundary_checks.physical_consequence: v_{AB} = v - (-u) = v + u (relative closing speed is the sum).

reconstruction_cycles.phenomenon: Newton-III Action-Reaction vs Single-Body Net Force
reconstruction_cycles.standard_derivation: Body A exerts force F_{A on B} on body B; body B exerts force F_{B on A} on body A. Third law states F_{A on B} = -F_{B on A}. Net force on body B is sum F_B = F_{A on B} + F_{ext on B} = m_B a_B.

phenomenological_reconstruction.conceptual_pivot: Equal-and-opposite forces can NEVER cancel each other unless they act on the EXACT SAME body. F_{A on B} acts on body B; F_{B on A} acts on body A. Because they live on separate free-body diagrams, they never enter the same net force equation.
phenomenological_reconstruction.resting_book_fallacy: A book resting on a table experiences downward gravity F_{Earth on book} and upward normal force F_{table on book}. These balance because sum F_{book} = 0 (first law), NOT because of the third law! Their third-law partners are F_{book on Earth} (upward on Earth) and F_{book on table} (downward on table).

limiting_boundary_checks.limit: Accelerating table (elevator accelerates upward with a)
limiting_boundary_checks.physical_consequence: Normal force becomes N = m(g + a) != mg; forces on book no longer balance, yet F_{table on book} and F_{book on table} remain strictly equal and opposite.
Normal force vanishes (N = 0); gravity accelerates book at g, with book pulling Earth upward with equal force mg.

reconstruction_cycles.phenomenon: Geometric Angle Control over Work Sign
reconstruction_cycles.standard_derivation: Force F acts on body while undergoing displacement s. Enclosed geometric angle is theta. Scalar work: W = F . s = |F||s| cos theta. cos theta > 0 for 0 <= theta < 90 deg; cos theta = 0 for theta = 90 deg; cos theta < 0 for 90 < theta <= 180 deg.

phenomenological_reconstruction.conceptual_pivot: Work is energy transferred by a force acting through a displacement. When force possesses a component along the direction of motion, it speeds the particle up (positive work, energy added). When force opposes motion, it slows the particle down (negative work, energy extracted). When force is strictly perpendicular, it only turns the particle without changing kinetic energy (zero work).
phenomenological_reconstruction.braking_invariant: A braking force acts opposite to displacement (theta = 180 deg), giving cos(180) = -1 and W = -F s. The negative sign represents kinetic energy dissipated into thermal energy.

limiting_boundary_checks.physical_consequence: cos(90) = 0 => W = 0 (e.g., centripetal tension, normal force on level surface).

cognitive_dissonance_probes.student_trap: A velocity of -15 m/s is smaller than a velocity of +5 m/s because negative numbers are smaller than positive numbers on a number line.
cognitive_dissonance_probes.socratic_challenge: If a car moving at -15 m/s crashes into a wall, does it cause less structural damage than a car moving at +5 m/s?
cognitive_dissonance_probes.resolution: No! Kinetic energy is proportional to speed squared (v^2). The car moving at -15 m/s carries 9 times the kinetic energy of the car at +5 m/s. The negative sign merely indicates the car travels West instead of East.

cognitive_dissonance_probes.student_trap: Adding a 6 N force and an 8 N force must always produce a 14 N force.
cognitive_dissonance_probes.socratic_challenge: What happens if one person pulls a rope to the right with 8 N and another pulls to the left with 6 N? What happens if they pull at right angles?
cognitive_dissonance_probes.resolution: Forces are vectors! They combine according to spatial geometry: R = sqrt(6^2 + 8^2 + 2(6)(8) cos theta). The resultant can be anything between 2 N (opposite) and 14 N (parallel). At right angles, R = 10 N.

cognitive_dissonance_probes.student_trap: A cyclist travels around a corner at a steady 6 m/s. Because the speedometer stays at 6 m/s, the change in velocity is zero.
cognitive_dissonance_probes.socratic_challenge: Is velocity just a speed number, or does it include heading? If you turn from East to North, did your direction change?
cognitive_dissonance_probes.resolution: Velocity includes direction! v_i = 6 i m/s and v_f = 6 j m/s. The change vector is Delta v = 6 j - 6 i m/s, with magnitude |Delta v| = 6 sqrt(2) m/s. Turning requires an inward sideways push.

cognitive_dissonance_probes.student_trap: If Cyclist A moves East at 8 m/s and Cyclist B moves East at 5 m/s, A sees B moving forward at 3 m/s.
cognitive_dissonance_probes.socratic_challenge: Cyclist A is traveling faster than Cyclist B. As A looks over their shoulder at B, is B getting closer or falling farther behind?
cognitive_dissonance_probes.resolution: B is falling behind! To find A's view of B, compute v_{B/A} = v_B - v_A = 5 - 8 = -3 m/s (3 m/s West). B appears to drift backward in A's frame.

cognitive_dissonance_probes.student_trap: A book rests on a table. The normal force pushes up and gravity pulls down with equal magnitude. Therefore, normal force and gravity are a Newton-III action-reaction pair.
cognitive_dissonance_probes.socratic_challenge: If you take the table away, gravity still pulls down on the book, but where did the normal force go? Can one partner of an action-reaction pair exist without the other?
cognitive_dissonance_probes.resolution: Never! Action-reaction partners must be of the same physical interaction type and act on different bodies. Normal force is a contact electromagnetic force (table on book <-> book on table). Gravity is a mass attraction (Earth on book <-> book on Earth).

cognitive_dissonance_probes.student_trap: Work is defined as force times distance, so pushing against a moving sled always adds energy and does positive work.
cognitive_dissonance_probes.socratic_challenge: If a sled slides toward you and you push against it to slow it down, does the sled speed up or lose kinetic energy?
cognitive_dissonance_probes.resolution: It loses kinetic energy! When force opposes displacement (theta = 180 deg), cos(180) = -1, and work is negative: W = -F s. Negative work removes kinetic energy from the system.
